files.title: TDD Best Practices
files.excerpt: Learn about TDD Best Practices in testing-validation.
files.content_html:
Test Design

  • Arrange Act Assert: Structure tests with Arrange-Act-Assert pattern for clarity
  • Single Responsibility: Each test verifies exactly one behaviour
  • Descriptive Naming: Test names describe what is being tested and expected outcome
  • Isolation: Tests must be independent and not share mutable state
  • Fast: Unit tests must run in milliseconds, not seconds

Workflow

  • Red Green Refactor: Follow Red-Green-Refactor cycle without skipping steps
  • Commit On Green: Commit after each Green phase to create safe checkpoints
  • Coverage Gate: Maintain minimum 80% line coverage before merging
  • Mutation Testing: Use mutation testing to verify test quality, not just coverage
  • Test Pyramid: More unit tests than integration tests than end-to-end tests

files.title: Clean Code Practices
files.excerpt: Learn about Clean Code Practices in backend-python.
files.content_html:
Naming

  • Meaningful Names: Use intention-revealing names; avoid abbreviations
  • Verb Functions: Function names should be verbs describing what they do
  • Noun Classes: Class names should be nouns representing domain concepts

Functions

  • Single Responsibility: Functions should do one thing and do it well
  • Small Functions: Functions should be small — ideally under 20 lines
  • No Side Effects: Prefer pure functions without hidden side effects
  • Command Query Separation: Functions either change state or return data, not both

Structure

  • Dry Principle: Don't Repeat Yourself — extract duplicated logic
  • Yagni Principle: You Aren't Gonna Need It — don't build speculative features
  • Boy Scout Rule: Leave the code cleaner than you found it
  • Dependency Injection: Inject dependencies rather than instantiating them
  • Fail Fast: Validate inputs early and return/raise promptly

files.title: Code Review Practices
files.excerpt: Learn about Code Review Practices in backend-python.
files.content_html:
Reviewer Mindset

  • Constructive Feedback: Provide actionable, specific feedback rather than vague criticism
  • Intent Understanding: Understand the intent of the change before critiquing implementation
  • Principle Based: Reference coding standards when requesting changes
  • Knowledge Sharing: Use reviews as teaching opportunities

Checklist

  • Correctness: Verify logic is correct and handles edge cases
  • Test Coverage: New code must have corresponding test coverage
  • Naming Clarity: Check names reveal intent
  • Error Handling: Ensure errors are handled gracefully
  • Security: Check for injection risks, authentication issues, data exposure
  • Performance: Flag O(n²) loops, unnecessary DB calls, memory leaks
  • Documentation: Verify public APIs have docstrings

Author Mindset

  • Small Prs: Keep pull requests small and focused on one concern
  • Self Review: Review your own diff before requesting review
  • Test First: Include tests in the same commit as implementation

files.title: Refactoring Techniques
files.excerpt: Learn about Refactoring Techniques in backend-python.
files.content_html:
Preconditions

  • Test Coverage First: Ensure adequate test coverage before refactoring
  • One Change At A Time: Apply one refactoring step at a time; verify tests pass
  • Commit Between Steps: Commit after each successful refactoring step

Techniques

  • Extract Method: Extract long code blocks into well-named helper methods
  • Rename Variable: Rename unclear variables/functions to reveal intent
  • Introduce Parameter Object: Replace long parameter lists with a value object
  • Extract Class: Move cohesive responsibilities to a dedicated class
  • Replace Conditional With Polymorphism: Use polymorphism instead of complex if/elif chains
  • Introduce Explaining Variable: Name complex expressions with intermediate variables
  • Remove Dead Code: Delete unused functions, variables, and imports

Validation

  • All Tests Pass: All existing tests must pass after each refactoring
  • No Behaviour Change: Refactoring must not alter observable behaviour
  • Coverage Maintained: Test coverage must not decrease

files.title: Secure Coding Practices
files.excerpt: Learn about Secure Coding Practices in security.
files.content_html:
Input Validation

  • Validate All Inputs: Validate and sanitise all external inputs — parameters, headers, body
  • Whitelist Approach: Use whitelist validation; reject anything not explicitly allowed
  • Parameterised Queries: Always use parameterised queries to prevent SQL injection

Authentication

  • Strong Passwords: Enforce strong password policies; hash with bcrypt/argon2
  • Mfa Required: Require multi-factor authentication for privileged operations
  • Session Management: Invalidate sessions on logout; use secure, HttpOnly cookies

Authorisation

  • Least Privilege: Grant minimum permissions required for the task
  • Check Every Request: Authorise every request, not just at login
  • Rbac: Use Role-Based Access Control for permission management

Secrets

  • No Hardcoded Secrets: Never hardcode secrets, API keys, or credentials in source code
  • Environment Variables: Load secrets from environment variables or secrets manager
  • Rotate Regularly: Rotate credentials and API keys on a regular schedule

Error Handling

  • No Stack Traces: Never expose stack traces or internal errors to end users
  • Log Securely: Log security events without logging sensitive data

files.title: Engineering Design Patterns
files.excerpt: Learn about Engineering Design Patterns in architecture.
files.content_html:
Creational

  • Factory Pattern: Use Factory to decouple object creation from usage
  • Singleton Pattern: Use Singleton sparingly; prefer dependency injection
  • Builder Pattern: Use Builder for complex object construction

Structural

  • Adapter Pattern: Use Adapter to integrate incompatible interfaces
  • Facade Pattern: Use Facade to simplify complex subsystem interactions
  • Decorator Pattern: Use Decorator to add behaviour without modifying the original class
  • Composite Pattern: Use Composite for tree structures and recursive hierarchies

Behavioural

  • Observer Pattern: Use Observer / Event Bus for decoupled event-driven communication
  • Strategy Pattern: Use Strategy to swap algorithms at runtime
  • Command Pattern: Use Command to encapsulate requests as objects
  • Chain Of Responsibility: Use Chain of Responsibility for flexible request processing pipelines

Selection

  • Pattern Necessity: Only introduce a pattern when it solves a concrete problem
  • Avoid Overengineering: Simple code without a pattern is better than complex code with one

files.title: SOLID Principles
files.excerpt: Learn about SOLID Principles in architecture.
files.content_html:
Solid

  • Single Responsibility: Single Responsibility — a class/module should have only one reason to change
  • Open Closed: Open-Closed — open for extension, closed for modification
  • Liskov Substitution: Liskov Substitution — subtypes must be substitutable for their base types
  • Interface Segregation: Interface Segregation — prefer small, specific interfaces over large general ones
  • Dependency Inversion: Dependency Inversion — depend on abstractions, not concretions

Cohesion

  • High Cohesion: Keep related responsibilities together; separate unrelated ones
  • Low Coupling: Minimise dependencies between modules
  • Encapsulation: Hide internal implementation details behind clean interfaces

Modularity

  • Package By Feature: Organise code by feature/domain, not by technical layer
  • Stable Dependencies: Depend on more stable modules; avoid circular dependencies
  • Explicit Contracts: Define module contracts with type hints and docstrings

files.title: Engineering Anti-Patterns
files.excerpt: Learn about Engineering Anti-Patterns in architecture.
files.content_html:
Structural Anti Patterns

  • God Object: Avoid God Objects that know too much or do too much
  • Spaghetti Code: Avoid tangled control flow; prefer linear, predictable execution
  • Lava Flow: Remove dead code rather than leaving it commented out
  • Golden Hammer: Avoid applying a single familiar pattern to every problem
  • Copy Paste Programming: Never copy-paste code; extract reusable abstractions instead

Process Anti Patterns

  • Big Ball Of Mud: Avoid incrementally growing an unstructured system; maintain clear architecture
  • Analysis Paralysis: Make decisions with available information; avoid indefinite planning
  • Premature Optimisation: Profile first; only optimise proven bottlenecks

Code Quality

  • Magic Numbers: Replace magic numbers and strings with named constants
  • Deep Nesting: Flatten deeply nested conditionals with early returns
  • Boolean Trap: Avoid boolean parameters; use enums or separate methods
  • Feature Envy: If a method uses mostly another class's data, move it there
  • Data Clumps: Combine frequently paired data items into a value object

Each bounded context has its own ubiquitous language and is independently deployable. ', 'when_to_use': ['Complex business logic with rich domain behaviour', 'Multiple teams working on the same codebase', 'Need to isolate domain changes from infrastructure'], 'key_concepts': [{'bounded_context': 'Explicit boundary within which a model applies'}, {'aggregate': 'Cluster of domain objects treated as a unit'}, {'domain_event': 'Something meaningful that happened in the domain'}, {'repository': 'Abstraction over data access within a bounded context'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Anemic domain model (behaviour-less data bags)', 'Shared database across bounded contexts', "Calling another context's repository directly"], 'cortex_usage': ['CORTEX orchestrators are bounded contexts (core/domain/support tiers)', 'Each orchestrator owns its data — no cross-orchestrator DB calls']}
  • {'id': 'ARC-002', 'name': 'Microservices Architecture', 'category': 'deployment', 'severity': 'high', 'description': 'Decompose the system into small, independently deployable services aligned to business capabilities. Services communicate via well-defined APIs. ', 'when_to_use': ['Independent scaling requirements per capability', 'Polyglot technology needs across services', 'Multiple teams deploying at different cadences'], 'key_concepts': [{'service_boundary': 'Owns a single business capability'}, {'api_contract': 'Stable interface between services (OpenAPI/gRPC)'}, {'circuit_breaker': 'Fault-tolerance pattern for inter-service calls'}, {'service_mesh': 'Infrastructure layer for service-to-service communication'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Distributed monolith (tight coupling disguised as services)', 'Synchronous chains longer than 3 services', 'Shared library containing domain logic'], 'cortex_usage': ['MCP server is a microservice boundary for external tool consumers', 'Orchestrators expose capabilities via IOrchestrator protocol']}
  • {'id': 'ARC-003', 'name': 'Event-Driven Architecture (EDA)', 'category': 'integration', 'severity': 'medium', 'description': 'Services communicate asynchronously via events. Producers emit events without knowing consumers. Enables loose coupling and temporal decoupling. ', 'when_to_use': ['Need for decoupled async workflows between components', 'Audit trail and event sourcing requirements', 'Fan-out patterns (one event, many consumers)'], 'key_concepts': [{'event_broker': 'Message bus (Kafka, RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus)'}, {'event_schema': 'Versioned contract for event payload'}, {'consumer_group': 'Set of consumers sharing load for an event type'}, {'dead_letter_queue': 'Events that failed processing after max retries'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Event-carried state transfer without schema registry', 'Direct DB reads in event handlers (coupling)', 'Unbounded event retention without compaction policy']}
  • {'id': 'ARC-004', 'name': 'CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)', 'category': 'data', 'severity': 'medium', 'description': 'Separate read (query) and write (command) models. Write model enforces business invariants; read model is optimised for query performance. ', 'when_to_use': ['Significantly different read vs write load profiles', 'Complex query requirements that would pollute the write model', 'Combined with Event Sourcing for full audit trail'], 'key_concepts': [{'command_handler': 'Validates + executes business operation, emits events'}, {'query_handler': 'Reads from denormalised read model, no side effects'}, {'read_model': 'Projection built from events, optimised for UI/API queries'}, {'event_store': 'Append-only log of all domain events'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Implementing CQRS without Event Sourcing for simple CRUD', "Sharing the write model's ORM entities in the read path"]}
  • {'id': 'ARC-005', 'name': 'Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)', 'category': 'structural', 'severity': 'high', 'description': 'Core domain logic is isolated from external concerns (DB, HTTP, MQ) via ports (interfaces) and adapters (implementations). Enables testing without infrastructure and swapping adapters without touching domain code. ', 'when_to_use': ['Need to test domain logic in isolation from infrastructure', 'Multiple delivery mechanisms (HTTP API + CLI + MQ consumer)', 'Anticipate swapping infrastructure (e.g., DB migration)'], 'key_concepts': [{'port': 'Interface defined by the domain (IRepository, IEventPublisher)'}, {'driving_adapter': 'Calls into the domain (HTTP controller, CLI command)'}, {'driven_adapter': 'Called by the domain (SQLAlchemy repo, Redis cache)'}, {'application_core': 'Pure domain + use cases, no infrastructure imports'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Importing ORM models into domain layer', 'Framework decorators on domain entities'], 'cortex_usage': ['IOrchestrator is a port; concrete orchestrators are driving adapters', 'ADOWorkItemProvider implements IWorkItemProvider port']}
  • {'id': 'ARC-006', 'name': 'Saga Pattern (Distributed Transactions)', 'category': 'integration', 'severity': 'medium', 'description': 'Manage long-running business transactions spanning multiple services without distributed locking. Each service performs a local transaction and emits an event/command; compensating transactions undo completed steps on failure. ', 'when_to_use': ['Multi-step workflows that must maintain consistency across services', 'Cannot use a 2-phase commit (e.g., across databases)', 'Long-running business processes with human approval steps'], 'key_concepts': [{'choreography': 'Each service reacts to events — no central coordinator'}, {'orchestration': 'Central saga orchestrator issues commands to services'}, {'compensation': 'Undo action executed when a step fails'}, {'saga_state': 'Durable state tracking which steps have completed'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Saga without compensation logic (partial failure = data inconsistency)', 'Synchronous saga steps (negates decoupling benefit)']}
  • {'id': 'ARC-007', 'name': 'Strangler Fig Pattern (Legacy Migration)', 'category': 'migration', 'severity': 'low', 'description': 'Incrementally replace legacy system by routing traffic to new implementation one capability at a time. Legacy and new coexist until full migration. ', 'when_to_use': ['Big-bang replacement is too risky', 'Need to deliver value while migrating', 'Legacy system must remain operational during migration'], 'key_concepts': [{'facade': 'Routes requests to legacy or new implementation'}, {'intercept': 'Capture and redirect specific legacy calls'}, {'incremental_cutover': 'Feature-by-feature migration with rollback'}], 'anti_patterns': ['Tight coupling between facade and both legacy and new implementations', 'Not measuring traffic split — unable to validate cutover']}

Guidance

  • implement_intents: ['Apply ARC-005 (Hexagonal) by default — domain logic must not import infrastructure', 'Use ARC-001 (DDD) bounded contexts to contain new features', 'Prefer ARC-003 (EDA) for cross-service integration over synchronous calls']

files.title: Monitoring and Observability
files.excerpt: Learn about Monitoring and Observability in devops-infrastructure.
files.content_html:
Pillars

  • Metrics: Collect quantitative measurements (latency, error rate, throughput)
  • Logs: Emit structured logs with correlation IDs for traceability
  • Traces: Use distributed tracing to track requests across services

Alerting

  • Slo Driven: Define SLOs first; alert only when SLO burn rate is critical
  • Avoid Alert Fatigue: Suppress low-signal alerts; ensure every alert is actionable
  • Runbooks: Link alerts to runbooks describing investigation steps

Instrumentation

  • Four Golden Signals: Monitor latency, traffic, errors, and saturation for every service
  • Cardinality Management: Limit label cardinality in metrics to control storage costs
  • Health Endpoints: Expose /health and /ready endpoints for platform integration

Analysis

  • Baseline Performance: Establish performance baselines before optimising
  • Anomaly Detection: Use statistical analysis to detect abnormal patterns
  • Capacity Planning: Use historical trends to forecast and plan capacity

files.title: Performance Profiling and Analysis
files.excerpt: Learn about Performance Profiling and Analysis in performance-optimization.
files.content_html:
Profiling

  • Measure First: Always profile before optimising; do not guess bottlenecks
  • Cpu Profiling: Use cProfile/py-spy to identify CPU hotspots
  • Memory Profiling: Use memory-profiler or tracemalloc for memory leak detection
  • Io Profiling: Profile I/O wait time separately from CPU time

Analysis

  • Amdahls Law: Speedup is limited by the serial fraction; parallelise judiciously
  • Big O Awareness: Understand algorithmic complexity before optimising constants
  • Database Explain: Use EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE on slow queries before adding indexes

Optimisation

  • Caching: Cache expensive computations at the appropriate layer
  • Connection Pooling: Use connection pools for databases and HTTP clients
  • Async Io: Use async I/O for network-bound operations to improve throughput
  • Batch Operations: Batch database writes to reduce round-trips
  • Lazy Evaluation: Defer expensive computations until results are needed
